changelog: FIXED, ALL FOUND ON A MAC: the storm no longer re-computes a blur on every tile on every frame — up to fifty of them at once, permanently, whenever a storm was on screen. The pulsing glows on bosses, raiders, the Command Power plate and the danger pill did the same thing on a smaller scale. None of them look any different; they simply stopped charging the graphics card rent. THE CARD COLLECTION OPENS INSTANTLY and scrolls without cards popping in row by row: every picture in the game is a local file, so nothing is loaded lazily any more — it is all decoded quietly while you sit in the menu, which took the collection from over a second of stutter to thirty milliseconds. NEW, UNDER SETTINGS: a GRAPHICS setting for machines that are struggling — an old laptop, or one driving a television. Balanced looks identical standing still and only stops effects that redo work every frame; Performance also stops things moving, so the board steps instead of gliding. Every cue and every sound still happens. And a FRAME-TIME METER under Debug, which shows what your display is actually managing — useful if the game ever feels heavy and you want to tell us something concrete. RENAMED: the Fire Swamp is now THE DEATH BOG and its rodents are BOG RATS. The secret finale is now THE LIVING HEART. Fourteen achievements have new names or new lines. Nothing about how any of it plays has changed by one tile or one hit point — the Death Bog is still a lethal maze of flame, poison and mire with one hidden way out, and the Living Heart still bleeds your HQ for every card you play and caps what you can carve off it each turn. These are our words now instead of borrowed ones, which is how it should have been from the start. Still universal and still notarized: one download runs natively on Intel and Apple Silicon, and opens with no Gatekeeper warning.
